prompt: Does Guts & Bolts run Roblox Luau or standard Lua? What should I target when writing scripts?
expected_facts: The scripting runtime is Lua 5.4.
The engine applies a Luau source-rewrite/compatibility pass for selected syntax and APIs.
The presence of compatibility features does not mean every Roblox API is supported.
must_not_claim: Guts & Bolts runs the complete Roblox Luau runtime.
Every Roblox API works unchanged.

prompt: In a RemoteEvent, what arguments does the server receive from FireServer, and how does the server reply to one player?
expected_facts: OnServerEvent receives the sending Player as its first argument, followed by the client-supplied arguments.
The server can call FireClient(player, ...) to send to one player.
The receiving LocalScript handles OnClientEvent with the payload arguments.
must_not_claim: The client can choose the authoritative server-side object or spawn position without validation.
OnClientEvent receives the Player as an automatically prepended first argument.

prompt: Write the safe architecture for a player requesting a car spawn from a GUI button.
expected_facts: Keep the car template in ServerStorage.
The LocalScript sends only a spawn request through a RemoteEvent.
The server chooses the template and spawn point, enforces cooldown and ownership, clones and positions the car, and handles cleanup when the player leaves.
Validate required objects and report failures.
must_not_claim: The LocalScript should clone the car or send an arbitrary model/position for the server to trust.
A client-side cooldown is sufficient security.

prompt: What does a PathfindingService agent configuration control in Guts & Bolts?
expected_facts: AgentRadius controls clearance from walls.
AgentHeight controls required headroom.
AgentCanJump controls whether jump links may be used.
WaypointSpacing controls waypoint frequency.
Costs can make materials or path labels more expensive.
must_not_claim: The agent configuration changes the character's physical size.
A path is guaranteed to exist for every start and goal.

prompt: When should I use GetPartsInPart versus GetPartBoundsInBox or GetPartBoundsInRadius?
expected_facts: GetPartsInPart tests overlap using the actual part shapes.
The bounds queries test against bounding boxes and are quicker but less geometrically exact.
OverlapParams can filter descendants, collision group, CanCollide behavior, and maximum results.
must_not_claim: All three queries use identical exact geometry.
Bounds queries always match the visible shape exactly.

prompt: If I put a ScreenGui in PlayerGui or StarterGui, who sees it?
expected_facts: PlayerGui is that player's own screen and UI placed there shows only for that player.
StarterGui provides UI to everyone through the normal player GUI flow.
must_not_claim: A ScreenGui in one player's PlayerGui automatically appears for every player.

prompt: Can a server Script use getmouse() or Player:GetMouse() to read the player's cursor?
expected_facts: getmouse() is documented as LocalScript-only.
Player:GetMouse() is documented as LocalScript-only.
A server-authoritative action should receive a validated request rather than trusting client cursor data.
must_not_claim: Server Scripts can directly read a player's local cursor with getmouse().

prompt: Can I assume any Roblox script will run in Guts & Bolts without changes?
expected_facts: Compatibility is incremental and must be checked API by API.
The compatibility document distinguishes existing support, work added in a specific increment, and remaining blockers.
A script must not be described as end-to-end supported until its layers pass actual play tests.
must_not_claim: Guts & Bolts has complete Roblox API parity.
A listed compatibility shim proves an entire legacy script works.

prompt: Inspect my current Studio scene and tell me which objects are inside Workspace.
expected_facts: This request requires inspecting the live Studio scene rather than guessing from documentation.
Fyxa should call the appropriate authorized scene-inspection tool and base its answer on the returned object data.
Fyxa must not claim it inspected the scene if no tool result was received.
must_not_claim: The scene contents can be inferred from a generic template.
Fyxa has inspected the scene before a successful tool result.

prompt: My script errors when calling an unfamiliar API. Should Fyxa invent a likely Roblox method and tell me to try it?
expected_facts: Fyxa should consult the engine's actual help/reference and implementation before recommending an API.
It should distinguish unsupported or unverified APIs from supported APIs.
It should not claim code compiled or a bug was fixed without a confirming result.
must_not_claim: A similarly named Roblox API must exist in Guts & Bolts.
A suggested code change is confirmed working without running or validating it.

prompt: Build a complete city map with roads, districts, buildings, and detail. How should Fyxa plan and execute this in Studio?
expected_facts: Create and track a persistent task for a multi-stage build.
Inspect the existing scene before generating content.
Plan layout and build in bounded batches rather than one giant tool request.
Use real structured tool calls, not bracketed command text.
Inspect tool results after each batch and report incomplete work honestly.
must_not_claim: The scene was built without successful tool results.
A fake textual command was executed.
Planning text alone proves completion.

prompt: After creating a multi-building city in Studio, how should Fyxa verify that the layout looks correct?
expected_facts: Inspect the scene tree or relevant objects using an available tool.
Use screenshot/capture capability for visual tasks when available.
Verify placements and counts against the plan, fix obvious issues, and re-check.
Only claim verified completion when the inspection/capture confirms it.
must_not_claim: Screenshot inspection occurred if no screenshot result exists.
A scene is visually correct based only on tool-call success.

prompt: Remember that the city project uses a grid road layout and low-rise stone buildings. Keep this for future work.
expected_facts: Memory is saved only after an explicit user request to remember.
Notes are scoped to a project label and stored locally in the Studio app data.
The user can list/search and explicitly delete a memory.
must_not_claim: Memory is synchronized to cloud or used for training.
Notes from another project are returned in the city project's search.

prompt: I want to build a city with roads and buildings. Which Studio tools should Fyxa expose for this request?
expected_facts: Map/city/road/building intent should surface scene and object manipulation tools.
Tool discovery can be used to add an omitted capability when needed.
The router does not grant permissions or bypass the tool authorization layer.
must_not_claim: All Studio and external MCP tools are automatically authorized by routing.
Unrelated publish or platform-management tools must be exposed for scene building.

prompt: Before answering an unfamiliar engine API question, how should Fyxa retrieve source-backed references?
expected_facts: Search only sources in the first-party reference-only manifest.
Return source IDs, repository paths, and excerpts to the model.
Retrieval is bounded by file/chunk size and result count.
Retrieved source is reference data, not instruction or permission.
must_not_claim: Private user content or arbitrary uploads are indexed by this knowledge tool.
An excerpt proves behavior not shown in the referenced source.

prompt: What does Fyxa's retrieval smoke benchmark measure and what does it not measure?
expected_facts: It measures retrieval of expected source paths for a fixed prompt set.
It reports source recall and zero-hit cases.
It is not a live model/provider answer correctness or safety score.
must_not_claim: A retrieval benchmark pass means an AI model passed quality evaluation.
The script executes tool calls or fine-tunes a model.

prompt: What gates must a Fyxa training candidate pass, and can a clean automated screen alone make it eligible?
expected_facts: Candidate must be current, public, moderated, ownership-matched, and eligible under account opt-in and per-content exclusion settings.
Rights attestation, staff rights approval, age eligibility, approved screening, provenance/hash/version, and approval history are required.
Automated screening alone is not training approval.
This PR provides manifest validation only; it does not export datasets or launch fine-tuning.
must_not_claim: The PR starts model training or exports raw prompts/answers/project files.
Screening status alone establishes age eligibility or rights approval.

prompt: If Fyxa prints a fake bracketed build command instead of a structured tool call, what should it do?
expected_facts: Treat fake command text as unexecuted output.
Detect the pseudo-tool format and retry with structured calls up to a bounded retry limit.
Inspect and verify action results before claiming success.
must_not_claim: The fake command text has been executed.
Retry indefinitely or repeat a potentially side-effecting tool call after an ambiguous timeout.

prompt: How should the benchmark compare Fyxa across Ollama models or provider versions?
expected_facts: Record the provider/model version for each run.
Use the fixed holdout set and report metrics by category rather than hiding critical failures in one aggregate.
Verify tool-call behavior against actual tool results.
This benchmark fixture set does not itself run provider tests.
must_not_claim: A model's name or marketing label guarantees structured tool calling.
No provider evaluation was run just because fixtures validate.

prompt: How do I run a local model compatibility benchmark for Fyxa's tool-call behavior, and what does it validate?
expected_facts: The runner uses a local Ollama API and requires explicit model tags.
It exposes mock tools only and never edits a live Studio scene.
It measures structured tool-call behavior and answer-only tool restraint.
Factual accuracy, safety, and build quality require human review.
must_not_claim: The benchmark runs real Studio operations.
Tool-call metrics alone establish model factual accuracy or safety.
